title: Is there an oilseed rape ideotype that can efficiently withstand sulfur deficiency?
content: This article comments on:D’Hooghe P, Kopriva S, Avice JC, Trouverie J. 2025. Tuning of sulfur flow and sulfur seed metabolism in oilseed rape under sulfate-limited conditions. Journal of Experimental Botany 76, https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/eraf028Oilseed rape (Brassica napus) is an economically important agricultural crop with a high concentration of sulfur (S) in its tissues and seeds, and a particularly high demand for S relative to its yield potential. Therefore, effective S management is a crucial part of oilseed rape production. In response to S restriction, oilseed rape increases S utilization efficiency to provide S for seeds. However, source–sink relationships and S management in developing seeds under S restriction are still poorly understood. D’Hooghe et al. (2025) have addressed the impacts of sulfate restrictions in the two genotypes, Capitol and Aviso, that are characterized by differences in S management under S deficiency. The authors elaborate on the physiological responses and provide a detailed description of the adaptation to S deficiency.
